questions.stem: What is the angle required to rotate an object around the x-axis by 90 degrees?
questions.solution: A rotation of 90 degrees around the x-axis is a quarter turn. Therefore, the correct angle is 90°.
questions.explanation: Rotating an object around the x-axis changes its position along the y and z axes while keeping the x-coordinate unchanged.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing 45° or 180° as they are not a quarter turn. The rotation must be exactly 90 degrees to meet the objective.

questions.stem: What is the equivalent positive angle for rotating an object around the x-axis by -270 degrees?
questions.solution: A negative angle can be thought of as a rotation in the opposite direction. To find an equivalent positive angle, add 360 degrees to -270 degrees.
questions.explanation: Rotating an object around the x-axis by -270 degrees is equivalent to rotating it clockwise by 90 degrees since adding 360° brings the object back to its original position along the y and z axes.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Subtracting 270° from 360°, which would result in a positive angle that is not equivalent. Remember to add 360° to convert a negative angle to a positive one.

questions.stem: An object is rotated around the x-axis by an angle of θ. Which of the following statements is true about the object's new position?

choices.C: Both the y- and z-coordinates remain unchanged.
choices.D: None of the coordinates remain unchanged.

questions.solution: When an object is rotated around the x-axis, only the y- and z-coordinates change. The x-coordinate remains constant.
questions.explanation: Rotation around the x-axis affects the position along the y and z axes while keeping the x-coordinate intact.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing B or C, assuming that both y- and z- coordinates remain unchanged. Only the x-coordinate remains constant during a rotation about the x-axis.

questions.stem: A 2D vector (1, 3) is rotated around the x-axis by 180°. What are the new coordinates of the vector?
questions.solution: Rotating a vector (1, 3) around the x-axis by 180° will result in a reflection across the x-axis. The y-coordinate changes sign while the x-coordinate remains unchanged.
questions.explanation: When rotating a vector around the x-axis, only the component perpendicular to the axis changes sign.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing B or D, assuming that both coordinates change signs or remain unchanged. Only the y-coordinate should change sign.

questions.stem: A 2x2 matrix [[1, 2], [3, 4]] is rotated around the x-axis by 90°. What is the new matrix?
questions.solution: Rotating a matrix around the x-axis by 90° is equivalent to swapping rows and columns and negating the elements in the new first column.
questions.explanation: Rotation of matrices can be performed using matrix multiplication with a rotation matrix. For a 90° rotation, the result will have the original second row as the new first row, and the original first row negated as the new second row.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Swapping rows without negating elements or vice versa. Remember to negate the elements in the new first column.

questions.stem: A rectangular prism is rotated around the x-axis by 180°. Which of the following statements is true about its new orientation?

choices.A: The front face remains facing forward.
choices.B: The top face remains facing up.
choices.C: Both the front and top faces remain in their original orientations.
choices.D: None of the faces maintain their original orientations.

questions.solution: Rotating a 3D object around the x-axis by 180° will cause all its faces to flip, so none of them will maintain their original orientation.
questions.explanation: A full rotation around any axis results in a complete change in orientation for a 3D object.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing A or B, assuming that certain faces remain unchanged. All faces will flip during a 180° rotation.

questions.stem: A point P(2, 4, 6) is described in a coordinate system rotated around the x-axis by 45°. What are the new coordinates of point P?
questions.solution: When the coordinate system is rotated around the x-axis by 45°, the new y and z coordinates can be found using trigonometric functions. The x-coordinate remains unchanged.
questions.explanation: Rotating a coordinate system affects how points are described in that system. To find the new coordinates of a point after rotation, use appropriate trigonometric relationships.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Applying the 45° angle directly to the original coordinates without using trigonometry. Remember to consider the effect of the rotated coordinate system.
